record.paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
record.context_brief: Simultaneous private access to multiple FSL submodels
record.original_question: In federated submodel learning, where a central learning model is divided into multiple submodels so each client downloads and updates only submodels relevant to that client’s local data, if a user has data for training multiple submodels at the same time, is there a private read/write method that lowers the total communication cost of reading and writing multiple submodels simultaneously compared with running the PRUW process separately for each submodel?

evidence.quote: One solution to this problem is federated submodel learning (FSL) [21]–[23], where the central learning model is divided into multiple submodels based on different types of training data, as this allows each client to only download and update the submodel(s) relevant to the client’s local data.

Private read-update-write (PRUW) [26]–[29] is the concept where a user downloads, updates and uploads the updates back to a chosen section of a data storage system, without revealing the content downloaded, uploaded or their positions, e.g., updated section index.

In a setting where a given user has a wide variety of data to train multiple submodels in FSL at the same time, it would be interesting to see if there exists any method that decreases the total communication cost of privately reading/writing to multiple submodels simultaneously, compared to carrying out the PRUW process on each submodel individually.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a federated submodel learning (FSL) system in which a global machine learning model is partitioned into M disjoint submodels W_1, …, W_M, each W_i consisting of L parameters taking values in a finite field F_q. The submodels are stored across N non-colluding databases using a (possibly coded) storage scheme. Users participate in training as follows: a user with locally available training data relevant to a subset S ⊆ {1, …, M} of the submodels wishes to (a) download the current values of all submodels W_i for i ∈ S (the read phase) and (b) upload an additive update Δ_i ∈ F_q^L to each W_i for i ∈ S so that the storage is updated to W_i + Δ_i (the write phase).

Privacy requirement (Private Read–Update–Write, PRUW). The protocol must guarantee that, from the messages exchanged with any single database, the database learns nothing (in the information-theoretic sense) about: (i) the index set S of submodels the user accesses, and (ii) the values of the uploaded updates {Δ_i : i ∈ S}.

Cost. Let C_read(|S|) and C_write(|S|) denote, respectively, the total number of symbols of F_q downloaded and uploaded by the user during the read and write phases of a PRUW protocol that serves a request of size |S|. Let C_PRUW^single denote the read+write communication cost of the best known PRUW protocol that handles a single submodel (|S| = 1).

Question. Does there exist a PRUW protocol that, when used by a single user to read and update |S| submodels simultaneously, achieves total read+write communication cost strictly less than |S| · C_PRUW^single — i.e., strictly less than the cost of running the single-submodel PRUW protocol |S| separate times — while still satisfying the information-theoretic privacy requirements above? Equivalently, characterize the optimal per-submodel communication rate (or capacity region) for simultaneous PRUW of |S| submodels and determine whether it improves upon the |S|-fold repetition baseline.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing PRUW literature (communication-efficient PRUW with/without sparsification, rate–distortion tradeoffs, heterogeneous databases, storage-constrained databases) all addresses the single-submodel-per-user setting. No published work was found that designs or characterizes the capacity of simultaneous PRUW for a user requesting multiple submodels at once, so the question of whether this beats |S|-fold repetition appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Private Read Update Write (PRUW) in FSL: Communication Efficient Schemes With and Without Sparsification
status_evidence.snippet: Each user downloads the required submodel without revealing its index in the reading phase, and uploads the updates of the submodel without revealing the submodel index or the values of the updates in the writing phase.
status_evidence.claim: Standard PRUW formulations treat a single required submodel per user.

status_evidence.title: Rate Distortion Tradeoff in Private Read Update Write in Federated Submodel Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how the communication cost of PRUW can be reduced when a pre-determined amount of distortion is allowed in the reading and writing phases.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work reduces PRUW cost via distortion but still in the single-submodel setting.

status_evidence.title: Information-Theoretically Private Federated Submodel Learning with Storage Constrained Databases
status_evidence.snippet: Develops read-write schemes for FSL that efficiently utilize available storage while minimizing total communication cost.
status_evidence.claim: Recent FSL communication-cost work focuses on storage constraints, not simultaneous multi-submodel requests.
